name: Joshua Rotenberg
body: I'm applying for the Customer Success Manager role because Juno is building AI around the real work of tax firms, which makes customer success a commercial growth engine rather than a support function. That is how I have operated across SaaS, MarTech, and agency environments: onboarding and adoption create the evidence for retention, executive trust surfaces expansion opportunities, and disciplined customer-health analysis keeps risk visible before it becomes churn. I now build that full lifecycle directly through Solenzo, including HubSpot and GoHighLevel architectures and AI-enabled workflows for B2B service businesses.

The evidence is concrete. At Birdeye I onboarded and managed 15-20 reseller partners with deal sizes of roughly $10K-$45K, retaining all but one, about 94%, while using utilization and customer-health metrics to identify adoption gaps and feeding prioritized customer feedback to Product and Engineering. At Wix I onboarded and launched 25+ clients per month, reached 120% of sales targets and 110% of implementation targets, and led the team responsible for launch and time-to-value; the e-commerce segment I supported saw a 30% increase in traffic and 25% improvement in conversion. Through Solenzo I own discovery, onboarding, reporting, lifecycle automation, and recommendations that expand retainer scope, including 20+ deployed workflows and daily use of ChatGPT and Claude to translate business intent into reliable systems.

I'm based in Arvada, Colorado, and am applying for the remote consideration noted in the posting. I would bring a commercial customer-success operating style, founder-level comfort building from the ground up, and a direct approach to executive relationships, customer risk, and expansion. Thank you for the consideration.
